MachineCreate.description:
A machine an operator is putting on the register.

``source_note`` is required for the same reason the SLA policy rows carry
one: every figure below is typed in from an organisation's own records, and
a screen full of costs with no stated origin is indistinguishable from a
screen full of invented ones.
MachineCreate.title: MachineCreate

MachineEvidenceOut.description: Tickets a person linked to this machine. Counted, never inferred.
MachineEvidenceOut.title: MachineEvidenceOut

RecommendationRequest.title: RecommendationRequest

ReplacementTableRow.title: ReplacementTableRow

RiskRadarRow.description: One open ticket with the numbers that decided where it sits in the list.
RiskRadarRow.title: RiskRadarRow

SlaPolicyPatch.description:
The business inputs a manager may edit (spec I.4).

Priority is absent because it identifies the row, and version is absent
because it is the system's counter: a manager who could type a version could
make an old recommendation look current.
SlaPolicyPatch.title: SlaPolicyPatch

SlaPolicyResponse.description:
One policy after an edit, with what the edit reaches.

``affected_ticket_ids`` are the open tickets of that priority which received
a ``POLICY_CHANGED_REFERENCE`` event. Their stored deadlines did not move;
the field exists so the interface can say truthfully which live work the
next recommendation will price differently.
SlaPolicyResponse.title: SlaPolicyResponse

TicketMachineLink.description:
Attach a ticket to a machine, or detach it.

A null ``machine_id`` clears the link. This is a person stating which
machine a ticket is about; nothing derives it, and dispatch never reads it.
TicketMachineLink.title: TicketMachineLink

TicketPatch.description:
The fields a dispatcher may correct after creation.

Priority is here and the deadline is not: changing a priority is a triage
decision that gets recorded as an event, while ``sla_due_at`` stays fixed at
the value the policy produced when the ticket was opened.
TicketPatch.title: TicketPatch

info.description: SLA-aware ticket allocation with an auditable decision history. Authentication, tickets, agents, the audit trail, recommendation, acceptance, override, manual rescore and Risk Radar.
info.title: SLA-aware service desk (the application)

put.description:
Set an agent's skills to exactly this list.

Replacement rather than merge: eligibility is decided by these rows, and a
skill that was removed has to actually disappear or the dispatcher would
keep seeing an agent proposed for work they no longer do.

post.description: Recommend, and only recommend. This endpoint assigns nobody (spec D.3).

get.description: The decision with its full candidate payload, for the audit view.

post.description:
Both the recommendation and the human's choice come back, so the client
can show the difference honestly rather than only the outcome.

get.description:
Liveness, the dialect, migration state, and which artifacts are loaded.

The model versions are here because the demo has to be able to answer "which
model produced that number?" without opening a database, and because a build
with no usable artifact should say so on its health endpoint rather than at
the first ticket creation.

patch.description:
Edit register figures.

Re-recording the age also re-stamps ``age_recorded_at``, so the advisor ages
the new figure forward from today rather than from whenever the row was
first written.

get.description: Who the cookie belongs to. The client uses this to restore its session.

Advice for the whole register, most overdue first.

The ordering is by how far past its optimal replacement year a machine is,
which is a number in the response rather than a judgement made here.

post.description: Group replacement against replace-on-failure for a fleet of like items.

patch.description:
Edit the business inputs for one priority (spec I.4).

The edit bumps ``version``, so every recommendation priced under the old
numbers becomes stale and must be rescored before it can be accepted. No
ticket's stored ``sla_due_at`` is touched, which is what the interface's
"affects future recommendations only" warning actually means.

post.description:
Record a human response to escalation. Nothing is routed anywhere.

This is the action Risk Radar offers on a flagged or overdue ticket. It
appends one immutable event and leaves the ticket's status, assignee and
deadline exactly as they were: the system recommends and records, and a
person decides what actually happens next (spec B.2).

get.description: History ascending by occurrence time, then event id (spec D.6).

put.description:
State which machine this ticket is about, or clear that statement.

This is the only way a ticket and a machine are ever connected. No column in
the source event log links an incident to an asset, so the link is a
person's assertion and the history records who made it. Nothing in scoring
or dispatch reads the field: linking a machine changes what the replacement
advisor counts, and nothing else.
